In a corner of the Black Wurtemberg Forest, in the rough casupola of a lumberjack. Federico Lœwe, after the unfortunate campaign of 1806, took refuge and hid with his mother, an old sick woman, and the two sisters Ricke and Jane: having declared Napoleon out of the war law all the volunteers who made the campaign under Lützow and Schill. Carlo Worms disappeared: lost to Saalfeld! And Chrysogono without his senior, discovered the refuge of Federico, one day he appears to you with his good smile to the newest of his senior, and a tear to the memory of his ex-senior, certainly dead. Germany now has more than a Kingdom of Westfalia and less his freedom. It is April, from the open window enter into the hut all the drunkenness of the spring, all the caresses of the forest, the Black Forest.

However, the walls are bizarrely covered with inscriptions and strange designs: flags, heads of death, the crossed arms of the Vehême, names, dates!... It is the third sunset, the last one, that surrounds the gloomy plain of Leipzig. Here the legend of the Germanic feud was won by this duel of giants that history already defines as the battle of nations.The fog of October as dense veil spreads over everything; it covers the sun, sky, horizon and envelops the vast land. Everything is grey, everything is invisible, everything merges into a vast indecisive set: Liebertwoolkwitz and Wachau and the woods of Gross-Posna. Far from Grimma the wind brings only the scalpitio of horses made furious and wild by terror; by Rochlitz screams of trumpets call the soldiers, lost, lost, errabonds; on from the field faint cries, faint prayers, groans of wounded and anguishes and spasms of dying!

In the plain of Leipzig, between Rochlitz and Grimma, on October 19, 1813. The battle, lasted three days, ended. On the camp never abandoned only the dead, the wounded, the forgotten. On the right is a embankment called the Thonberg, where it was fought fiercely: from there Napoleon witnessed the battle. On the Thonberg there was a tobacco mill: now there are nothing but ruins, destroyed caries, cannons disassembled, broken wheels, ruins of men and things everywhere; a misery; the terror. The mix of uniforms and colors is bizarrely and funerally fused in blood and mud; the uniforms of Merveldt, of Lichtenstein, of the partisans of Thielman and the brown ones of Lützow are confused with those of the Cossacks of Platoff, of Rajewsky's grenadiers and the blues of the great Guardia of Napoleon and of the hunters of Leuetzow are confused with those of the Greater-Des of the Krafettes, of the Krajs-D
